STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm; this one looks like a medium-large dinner plate, so about 26 cm.
b) Reference: the grapes are about 2.2 cm. The food cluster (roughly 9 grapes across the right edge) spans a fraction of the plate. The plate's width spans roughly 12-13 grape-lengths across the visible inner area... taking the plate edge-to-edge at about 11-12 grapes wide gives roughly 25-27 cm.
Reconciled width: 26 cm, so area = 26 x 26 = 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Potato cubes (roasted/fried): occupy about 22% of the plate area ≈ 149 cm². Pile is chunky, 2 cubes high at the thickest point, cube about 2 cm, so peak ~4 cm, average ~2 cm. Volume = 149 x 2 = 298 ml. Density 1.0 (mash/potato-like, fried) → about 300 g... using a more conservative density for cubed potato (~0.7) gives ~210 g.
- Grapes: visible ~11, plus hidden ones beneath ~4, total ~15 x 5 g = 75 g.
- Watermelon: 5 pieces, each roughly 3 x 3 x 2 cm ≈ 18 ml, total ≈ 90 ml x 0.6 = 54 g. Hmm, pieces are larger on the plate; using ~4 cm × 3 cm × 1.5 cm ≈ 18 ml each, 5 pieces ≈ 54 g.
- Feta/white cheese dab on potatoes: ~2 cm blob x 0.5 cm ≈ 1 ml → about 2 g (small). Cheese on the side plate is not counted, as it is on another vessel.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: a base layer under the potatoes is not clearly visible; no extra hidden layer assumed beyond the grapes already counted.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Fried/roasted potato: about 150 kcal/100 g.
- Grapes: about 69 kcal/100 g.
- Watermelon: about 30 kcal/100 g.
- Feta-type cheese: about 260 kcal/100 g.

Totals: potato ~210 g (315 kcal), grapes ~75 g (52 kcal), watermelon ~54 g (16 kcal), cheese ~2 g (5 kcal). Total ≈ 341 g, ≈ 388 kcal.
